# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [date I am sending this letter]

**To:** BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina
Appeals Department — address listed in the appeal rights section of my Explanation of Benefits

**From:** Riley Lawson
Member ID: W142769926
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-25 — Reference number POC-3E3F8049CD-32778**
**Service denied:** Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
**Member:** Riley Lawson, ID W142769926
**Claim/authorization number:** [claim or authorization number, if one appears on my EOB]

---

## The policy I am asking you to apply

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my total ankle replacement (CPT 27702). The plan's own published medical policy for this surgery is **Total Ankle Replacement CAM 70177**, available at https://www.southcarolinablues.com/web/public/brands/medicalpolicy/external-policies/total-ankle-replacement/ (reviewed 2024-12-11). Every piece of plan language I quote below is taken word for word from that policy.

## What the denial says, and why I am asking you to look again

The notice dated 2026-08-25 denied my request on the ground that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. The notice does not identify which document was missing, which criterion could not be evaluated, or what additional record would have answered the question. I am asking for reconsideration because the material my surgeon submitted does address the plan's stated criteria, and I am listing it below item by item so that a reviewer can match the records to the policy directly. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

**1. The threshold criterion — pain that limits daily activity.**

The policy states:

> "Total ankle replacement using an FDA approved device may be considered MEDICALLY NECESSARY in skeletally mature patients with moderate to severe ankle (tibiotalar) pain that limits daily activity"

My records establish this. The prior authorization packet documents 14 months of progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest. My weight-bearing ankle radiographs of 2026-06-18 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts — findings in the tibiotalar joint the policy names. On examination I have positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. My daily activity is limited: I walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks.

The packet also documents that I did not arrive at surgery quickly. I completed supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance — 16 weeks, 24 visits, from 2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note. I took NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19 gave me only three weeks of partial relief.

**2. The additional conditions the policy lists.**

The excerpts of the policy available to me include the following as alternatives:

> "Arthritis in adjacent joints (i.e., subtalar or midfoot); OR"

> "Severe arthritis of the contralateral ankle; OR"

> "Arthrodesis of the contralateral ankle; OR"

> "Inflammatory (e.g., rheumatoid) arthritis"

> "In general, patients selected for arthroplasty would not be good candidates for arthrodesis due to the presence of bilateral or subtalar arthritis or Chopart arthrosis."

I want to be straightforward with you: these are diagnostic findings that live in my surgeon's chart and imaging interpretation, not in anything I can supply myself, and the summary I have does not tell me which of them my reviewer looked for. The policy also appears to list further conditions that were not reproduced in the excerpts available to me. If the determination turned on one of these items, that is exactly the kind of specific request that would let my surgeon respond, and I am asking you to identify it in writing so that Dr. Okafor can send the relevant records. I would also ask you to confirm that Dr. Okafor's operative records and imaging report were reviewed in full, since a denial for incomplete documentation should identify the gap it found.

**3. Candidate and rehabilitation considerations.**

The policy states:

> "Optimal candidates for total ankle replacement are considered to be older (age > 50), thin, low-demand individuals with minimal deformity."

> "Patients should have no funcitonal barriers to participation in a rehabilitation program."

On the points my records do address: my BMI is documented as 29, I am a non-smoker, and the packet records no active infection and no untreated substance use. My ability to participate in rehabilitation is not a theoretical question — I already completed 24 supervised physical therapy visits over 16 weeks, which is direct evidence that I have no functional barriers to a rehabilitation program. As to age, my date of birth is on file with the plan; my age at the time of the request is [my age]. I would note that the policy frames this sentence as a description of optimal candidates rather than as a list of pass/fail thresholds, and it states no numeric requirement for weight, activity level or deformity that I could be measured against.

The policy also states:

> "Ankle arthroplasty should be performed by surgeons who are adequately trained and experienced in the specific techniques and devices used"

My surgery is planned with Dr. Okafor, MD, a physician in orthopedic surgery. [Any documentation of Dr. Okafor's training or experience with the specific device, if the plan requires it.]

**A note on thresholds.** I have quoted the plan's language exactly and I have not assumed any minimum duration of conservative care, any required number of therapy visits, any radiographic grade, or any other numeric cutoff, because the policy text available to me does not state one. If the plan applied such a threshold in reaching this determination, that threshold is not in the language I have, and I ask that it be identified and quoted in the appeal response.

## Please send me the criteria that were actually applied

I am asking, as part of this appeal, that the plan provide me in writing the complete clinical review criteria that the reviewer used to decide my case, including any criteria used by a delegated reviewer rather than the plan itself. I understand that BlueCross BlueShield of South Carolina uses Evolent for musculoskeletal surgery review, and that Evolent publishes its criteria publicly at no cost and without a login. The plan and its reviewer hold that document; I do not. Please identify the exact criteria set and version applied to reference number POC-3E3F8049CD-32778, and the specific criterion that my documentation was found not to satisfy. Without that, I cannot know what record to supply, and neither can my surgeon.

## What I am asking for

I ask that you overturn the denial dated 2026-08-25 and approve CPT 27702 as medically necessary under Total Ankle Replacement CAM 70177. If you cannot approve it on the records already submitted, I ask that you state precisely which document or finding is missing, so that Dr. Okafor can provide it, and that you keep my appeal open while that material is obtained. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with training in orthopedic surgery.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-21**, and I am submitting it in writing before that date. I am sending it by mail to the appeals address listed in the appeal rights section of my Explanation of Benefits. If I have used the wrong address, please forward this appeal to the correct department and let me know. If the plan has questions, the Customer Service number on the front page of my EOB is the line I can be reached about, and my direct number is above.

**Enclosed:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-25 (reference POC-3E3F8049CD-32778)
- Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03, 24 visits
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report, 2026-06-18
- Office notes and letter of medical necessity from Okafor, MD [to be provided by my surgeon's office]
- [Designation of Authorized Representative form, if someone is filing on my behalf]

Thank you for taking another look at this. I want to get back to walking more than two blocks, and I would like that decision made against the plan's own written criteria.

Sincerely,

**Riley Lawson**
Member ID: W142769926
[Signature]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
